requirements.requirement: node1 (VyOS) serves DHCP addresses to node3 on lan-a, with node1 itself as the default gateway
requirements.summary: node1 eth2 set to 10.50.10.1/24 and Kea DHCPv4 configured with subnet 10.50.10.0/24, pool .100-.200, default-router 10.50.10.1. Kea confirmed active (cmd-e941c482561e45b2). node3 dynamically acquired 10.50.10.100/24 with default route via 10.50.10.1 both before (cmd-97a6710767544a6c) and after (cmd-daa71bf042eb46ad) node1's restart, confirming persistence.

requirements.requirement: node2 (OPNsense) serves DHCP addresses to node4 on lan-b, with node2 itself as the default gateway
requirements.summary: After discovering a port conflict between Kea and dnsmasq (the pre-existing running DHCP backend), the executor reverted the Kea attempt and configured dnsmasq on opt1/vtnet2 (10.50.20.1/24, dhcp-range 10.50.20.100-.200). node4 dynamically acquired 10.50.20.135/24 with default route via 10.50.20.1, confirmed both pre-restart (cmd-e59383b42ca247e1, cmd-1c6d5daedeec4588) and post-restart (cmd-d0a2b09368b94da3), with dnsmasq confirmed running on port 67 after reboot (cmd-3a4f1f633c1b46fb).

requirements.requirement: node3 and node4 obtain their addressing dynamically from the router in front of them rather than via static configuration
requirements.summary: Both node3 and node4 have NetworkManager ipv4.method=auto on their segment-facing interface (eth1), with no static addresses/gateway configured. Actual DHCP lease acquisition and default-route installation from the correct router was directly observed both before and after each node's restart.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied with direct evidence: node1 (VyOS) serves DHCP on lan-a via Kea with itself as gateway, node2 (OPNsense) serves DHCP on lan-b via dnsmasq with itself as gateway (after correcting an initial Kea/dnsmasq port conflict), and both node3 and node4 obtain dynamic addressing with correct default routes from their respective routers. The mandatory provider-wide restart protocol was completed for all four nodes with clear pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity (cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots), and recovered service/client state. Hygiene is good overall; the only notable friction was bounded, fully-reverted point-to-point test addressing during topology discovery and a reverted Kea DHCPv4 attempt on node2 before settling on dnsmasq, none of which left residue in the final state.
limitations: The transcript for node2's Kea-vs-dnsmasq troubleshooting is dense with configuration introspection; while the final state clearly shows only dnsmasq active and Kea disabled, the intermediate 125s timeout on cmd-2fd9cfefc40741db means the exact intermediate state during that failed command is not fully captured, though it does not affect the final observed outcome.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor performed extensive but largely bounded troubleshooting. It temporarily assigned test point-to-point addresses (192.0.2.x) on node1 eth1/eth2, node2 vtnet1/vtnet2, and node3/node4 eth1 to map physical L2 topology (e.g. cmd-a699866b4c554767, cmd-76b6af578ecf4570, cmd-e357f051378e4b8d, cmd-30e8b10036d74c05, cmd-559b29696f9e4455, cmd-74da1ab9fa974f74, cmd-57484469cfb74b23, cmd-95d87c2a1c28433e, cmd-2df51f542f664f53, cmd-ba87d5178f0c4207) — all of these addresses were removed/reverted by cmd-8d1ce8fada7448cd, cmd-119c178e7e5947c6, cmd-e362fe0981144493, cmd-188df8ff77a1472d before final configuration, and final interface state shows no residue. On node2, the executor first attempted to enable Kea DHCPv4 for lan-b (cmd-a73bb2e215ad44a3, cmd-b173174a46704ed9, cmd-98e6020f911f4e23), which caused a port-67 bind conflict with the pre-existing dnsmasq service (confirmed in cmd-182710bdbacf43e9 log); this was a reasonable initial attempt given ambiguity in OPNsense's DHCP backend, and was fully corrected by stopping Kea and disabling it again (cmd-dadfc5538bee46e7, cmd-2f705c5bebaf4e36) before configuring dnsmasq instead, leaving no residual conflicting service (post-restart state shows only dnsmasq listening on port 67). One command during this sequence (cmd-2fd9cfefc40741db) failed with a 125s proxy timeout while running kea_sync/kea start; its effects were absorbed into the later cleanup and did not leave residue. No unnecessary mutations remained in the final state; hygiene is reduced modestly for the volume of exploratory read/write cycling on node2's DHCP backend rather than for any lasting negative effect.
